summary: A complete, carefully engineered Stage 4: correct chassis geometry (deck 0.540, keybed 0.460, width 0.940, aspect 3.0951, worst section deviation 0.0058), an exact 73-key E1-E7 keybed (43/30, black-key height 0.610, all keys inside), 5/5 reference colours inside deltaE 12, 156/156 controls reachable at 1440x900 and 32/33 landmarks present. Three genuinely different engines reach audio — piano samples, six distinct organ models with working drawbars/percussion/vibrato, 13 of 14 distinct synth waveforms with a working filter, envelopes and LFO — and every effect unit was measured against every engine. Programs, Live Mode, splits, zones, scenes, morphs, transpose and panic all round-trip and reach the signal. Three defects hold it back. The Rotary unit is stripped from the per-voice render as 'live' but no rotary node is ever built, so its LEDs light while the rendered signal is bit-identical; the unit tests only cover the offline path. Every fresh note-on blocks the main thread 49-109 ms pre-rendering 8 s of audio, and that 8 s ceiling cuts held organ notes dead. The arpeggiator can only run off a stale config snapshot, so it never arpeggiates in normal play.

evidence: Three genuinely different engines, measured on rendered signal at the destination (AudioNode.prototype.connect tap, after a warm-up note so the sample library was loaded). Piano C4 vs organ C4: log-spectrum correlation 0.13 over 32 log-spaced bands. All six organ models differ from one another (B3 vs Vox 72 dB apart at 1.6 kHz, B3 vs Farf 66 dB at 6.4 kHz, B3 Bass vs B3 40 dB at 400 Hz; Pipe 1 vs Pipe 2 differ by 7 dB, consistent with the spec's 'same engine, brighter registration').

13 of the 14 synth waveforms render distinct spectra. The one coincidence is FM 2-op A vs Sine (log-correlation 1.00, max band delta 0.64 dB) and it is correct rather than a stub: OSC CTRL is the FM index and its default is 0, so the 2-op FM collapses to its carrier sine. White Noise is genuinely noise (rms 0.0373 vs 0.0768 for Saw with a flat spectrum), and the Multi/Super stacks differ from their single-oscillator siblings (Super Saw rms 0.0254 vs Saw 0.0768).

Deductions a knowledgeable player would hear: every voice is a fixed 8-second pre-render, so a held organ note — which should sustain indefinitely — dies dead at ~8s (measured: 10s hold, envelope non-zero through bucket 16 of 22 then exactly 0 while the key was still down). The 'recorded' piano library is this project's own physical model bounced to WAV rather than a recorded instrument (declared truthfully in IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json, and the 108 WAVs really are fetched and decoded — /samples/grand/28_pp.wav etc. appear in the network log).

One AudioContext and a real shared graph: the connect census shows GainNode->DynamicsCompressorNode->AudioDestinationNode (master -> limiter -> destination), 6 GainNode->ConvolverNode reverb sends, ConvolverNode->GainNode return, and per-voice AudioBufferSourceNode->GainNode. Every unit was A/B'd against each engine with FX FOCUS on that engine: delay (piano rms x0.16, organ x0.07, synth x0.07), reverb (max band delta 20/74/21 dB), Effect 1 (73/59/25 dB), Effect 2 (23/63/34 dB), amp+drive (x5.03/x4.18/x4.13), compressor (x0.57/x0.70/x0.71), EQ treble (45/89/29 dB). No engine is left out of the chain.

The Rotary unit, however, is not in the shipped signal path at all. web-audio-backend.ts renders each voice through renderGraph(withoutLiveUnits(effects)), and withoutLiveUnits sets clone.rotary.on = false and rewrites amp type 6 ('To Rotary') to type 0, on the stated grounds that rotary 'stays a live node' — but the backend constructor builds only master, limiter, six layer gains, six reverb sends, one convolver and one return. There is no DelayNode, OscillatorNode, StereoPannerNode or WaveShaperNode anywhere in the live graph.

Measured consequence: with the organ soloed, ORGAN routing on, fx.rotaryOn on and speed cycled SLOW -> STOP -> FAST, the rendered signal was rms 0.0732745 / peak 0.1637178 for the dry take and rms 0.0732745 / peak 0.1637178 for every rotary take — identical to seven decimal places; the band vectors correlate at 1.00 with a worst-band delta of 1.94 dB (recording-alignment noise). The rotary tests in src/__tests__/effects-processing.test.ts and effects-graph.test.ts assert only against renderWith()/renderGraph, the offline path that keeps rotary on, so they stay green over a browser path that discards it.

Each note-on synchronously renders 8 seconds of audio through the whole graph on the main thread. Measured around real note-ons in the page: 108.6, 69.2, 80.2, 48.8, 64.4, 57.3, 60.0 ms for fresh (note, velocity, config) combinations, and 0.2-0.4 ms once the buffer cache (96 entries) hits. A PerformanceObserver longtask of 52 ms was also recorded. Because pointer velocity is derived from the strike position it varies continuously, so real playing mostly misses the cache.

Under a heavy load it stays stable but sluggish: 15 keys held with piano+organ+synth all enabled rendered rms 0.2684 with peak 0.9606 (no clipping past 1.0; the DynamicsCompressor limiter holds), no console errors and rAF latency back to 0.2 ms afterwards — but pressing those 15 keys took 3953 ms of wall time for a 1500 ms hold.

Voice lifecycle is otherwise sound: 1/3/10 simultaneous keys gave rms 0.0492 / 0.0826 / 0.1258, PANIC left rms exactly 0, space-bar sustain produced a decaying tail after key-release where the un-sustained note ended at 0, and MIDI CC64 sustain behaved the same. The 8-second render ceiling also caps any held note (organ measured cutting out at ~8 s).

Full round-trip driven in the build: changing piano type raised the dirty flag in the program OLED ('1.1 Grand Piano E' and 'Piano A: Grand Upright'), STORE opened the flow line 'STORE → 1.1 (STORE=ok · SHIFT=cancel)', the second STORE cleared the dirty E, moving to program 3 showed '1.3 B3 Jazz' and returning to program 1 showed '1.1 Grand Piano' with 'Piano A: Grand Upright' — the stored edit survived the round-trip and the dirty flag was truthful at every step.

Page navigation and Live Mode work: PAGE-right then program 1 loaded '2.1 Split Bass/Piano', PAGE-left then program 1 returned to '1.1 Grand Piano', and LIVE MODE showed 'Live 1 Init' and restored the program slot on exit. The canonical schema in src/state/program-state.ts stores piano/organ/synth/effects/split/scene/morph/clock/transpose on integer panel scale with Master Level deliberately excluded, and persists through an injected storage seam.

All three input paths reach one note lifecycle in the build: a real pointer press on a key rendered audio (rms 0.060), the mapped computer keys played (Q/E/T chord rms 0.0826) and space sustained after focus was cleared (tail 0.0076 decaying to 0.00005 after key-release, against an exactly-zero tail without it). Web MIDI reports 'denied' in headless Chromium, so I stubbed navigator.requestMIDIAccess: the status bar then read 'MIDI: ready', a 0x90/0x80 note pair rendered rms 0.0480 and CC64 held the note after note-off.

Performance bindings behave: PANIC left rms exactly 0 with a key still down; TRANSPOSE moved the OLED to 'TR +1' and shifted the rendered spectrum (log-correlation 0.48, 72.6 dB at 1.13 kHz); assigning the mod wheel to piano.level lit [data-morph-led="piano.level"] and driving the wheel to 127 changed the rendered note from rms 0.0490 to 0.0415. The seven spec-excluded controls (program.morphAftertouch, program/organ panel A/B select, piano.modelSelect, synth.oscMix) are rendered without data-functional and are named in the status bar, which matches the honesty contract.

Held back from 4 because the rotary SLOW/STOP/FAST and DRIVE bindings move and light their LEDs without changing the signal at all, and the FX FOCUS A/B buttons do not follow the engine's focused layer.

Splits gate real audio. With SPLIT on (Mid point at C4, split LEDs and the zone strip showing 'Zone 1 (E1–C4)' / 'Zone 2 (C4–E7)'), C3 rendered rms 0.0496 and C5 rendered 0.0440; after arming KB ZONE and reassigning the focused piano layer off zone 1, C3 fell to exactly 0 while C5 stayed at 0.0440, and undoing the assignment restored it.

Layer Scenes round-trip: from Scene I (piano A on, B off) I switched to Scene II and enabled layer B; returning to Scene I restored A on / B off, and returning to Scene II restored B on. Scene I and Scene II also rendered different audio (log-correlation 0.69, 58 dB at 84 Hz). Transpose and PANIC were verified above and act globally through engine state rather than per section.

Held at 3 because I could only measure transpose, panic and split gating against the piano layers; with all three engines enabled at once the workflows behaved but the 3953 ms cost of a 15-note chord makes simultaneous cross-engine play unpleasant.

Drawbars, models, percussion and vibrato all reach audio. Pulling drawbar 9 (1') from 0 to 8 raised the 1.6 kHz band by 35.6 dB. All six models (B3, B3 Bass, Vox, Farf, Pipe 1, Pipe 2) render measurably different spectra and the section label tracks them ('A: B3' ... 'A: Pipe 2'). Percussion changed the attack (first two 75 ms envelope buckets 0.0060/0.0749 without it, 0/0 then 0.0280/0.0933 with it) and added 50.4 dB at 1.9 kHz. VIB/CHORUS on changed the spectrum (log-correlation 0.73). Octave shift, layer A/B, level fader, SUST PED and P STICK routing are all present and wired.

Rotary — one of the five things this criterion names — is inert. The organ's ROTARY routing button plus fx.rotaryOn plus SLOW/STOP/FAST produced a rendered signal identical to the dry take (rms 0.0732745 both, peak 0.1637178 both, band correlation 1.00), because the browser backend strips rotary from the per-voice render and never builds it as a live node.
The Rotary Speaker block is also missing from the performance band where the reference photograph puts it, so the organ's rotary hardware is neither in the right place nor audible anywhere.

Oscillators, filter, envelopes, LFO and unison all reach audio and are individually measurable: 13/14 waveforms spectrally distinct; filter cutoff min vs max log-correlation 0.49 with rms 0.0411 vs 0.1212; the four filter types mutually distinct (LP12 vs HP correlation -0.18); resonance at max lifted rms to 0.1351; amp attack at max produced a genuine ramp (envelope 0, 0.000008, 0.00078, 0.00198, 0.00323 ...) against an instant 0.1218 at minimum; LFO to Filter at full amount changed the spectrum by 51.5 dB at 566 Hz versus amount 0; UNISON 3 raised rms from 0.121 to 0.177.

The arpeggiator is implemented and can be made to arpeggiate — with KB HOLD populating the pool with C3 and C5 and a panel change afterwards, per-100 ms Goertzel tracking of 130.8 Hz and 523.3 Hz alternated cleanly — but it never runs in ordinary play. The rendered arp pool comes from cfg.arpNotes, which is only refreshed by PianoEngine.pushConfig() on a state change; noteOn never pushes config, so pressing ARP RUN and then playing a note or a chord renders an ordinary sustained voice. Measured: with ARP RUN on, a 3 s held note gave the same single-pulse envelope and peak (0.0934) as with it off, and the arp rate knob at minimum vs maximum changed the pulse count only from 2 to 1.

Gate mode has its own defect: with the pool populated and ARP/GATE rate at 127 the rendered output was digital silence for the whole 3 s hold (every 5 ms envelope bucket exactly 0), while the same setup at the default rate 90 gated correctly at 3.6 Hz.

Layers, splits, scenes and morphs all reach audio and state. Seven routable layers exist (pianoA/B, organA/B, synthA/B/C) on six buses; splits offer 3 points over the 11 documented positions with Off/±6/±12 crossfades and up to 4 zones, and zone reassignment measurably silenced C3 (rms 0.0496 -> 0) while leaving C5 untouched.

Scenes store and restore per-layer enables (I: A on/B off; II: A on/B on; verified across two round-trips) and render different audio. Morphs work end to end: holding MORPH ASSIGN WHEEL and moving piano.level recorded the destination (green [data-morph-led="piano.level"] lit) and driving the wheel from 0 to 127 changed the rendered note from rms 0.0490 to 0.0415. Aftertouch is spec-excluded and is declared unsupported rather than faked.

32 program slots on 4 pages plus 8 Live slots, all driven from the panel: the dirty 'E' indicator appeared on edit and cleared on store, the STORE flow rendered its confirm line, slot recall preserved the stored edit, PAGE ◀ ▶ plus a program button loaded '2.1 Split Bass/Piano' and returned to '1.1 Grand Piano', and LIVE MODE showed 'Live 1 Init' with auto-store and restored the program slot on exit.

The OLED is the real display for all of it — position, name, dirty flag, store destination, split edit line, clock/transpose/scene line — and a Shift+dial list view of all 32 slots exists in the code path behind data-oled-mode="list".

issues.title: Rotary speaker is absent from the shipped signal path while the panel reports it engaged
issues.detail: src/audio/web-audio-backend.ts renders every voice through renderGraph(withoutLiveUnits(effects)); withoutLiveUnits forces clone.rotary.on = false and rewrites amp type 6 ('To Rotary') to type 0, on the comment 'reverb + rotary stay live nodes'. But the backend's live graph contains only master gain, limiter, six layer gains, six reverb sends, one convolver and one return — the connect census at the destination shows no DelayNode, OscillatorNode, StereoPannerNode or WaveShaperNode anywhere. Measured with the organ soloed and ORGAN routing + fx.rotaryOn on, cycling SLOW/STOP/FAST: rms 0.0732745 and peak 0.1637178 for the dry take and for every rotary take, band correlation 1.00. The ON and SLOW/FAST LEDs light and IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json states 'Organ routes to the shared Rotary via the ORGAN button ... rotary speed ramps (acceleration), and Stop mode silences the modulation', so the artifact declares and displays an effect that never touches audio. The unit tests that cover rotary (effects-processing.test.ts, effects-graph.test.ts) assert only against the offline renderGraph path, which keeps rotary on, so they stay green over the defect.

issues.title: Every fresh note-on blocks the main thread 49-109 ms rendering 8 s of audio
issues.detail: WebAudioBackend.startVoice calls bufferFor(), which synchronously renders RENDER_SECONDS = 8 of audio through the entire graph before the note can start. Measured around real note-ons in the published build: 108.6, 69.2, 80.2, 48.8, 64.4, 57.3, 60.0 ms (0.2-0.4 ms on a buffer-cache hit; the cache is keyed on note+velocity+full config and holds 96 entries, and pointer velocity varies continuously with strike position so real playing mostly misses it). A 52 ms longtask was recorded by PerformanceObserver. Playing a 15-key chord with all three engines enabled took 3953 ms of wall time for a 1500 ms hold.

issues.title: Held notes stop dead at 8 seconds because each voice is a fixed pre-render
issues.detail: Voices are AudioBufferSourceNodes over an 8-second buffer with no loop, so any sustained voice ends at 8 s regardless of the key. Measured with the organ soloed and a key held 10 s: the 5 ms envelope carried signal through ~8 s and then read exactly 0 for the remaining ~2 s while the key was still down. An organ that stops sounding while the key is held is a musical failure a player notices immediately; the same ceiling applies to synth pads.

issues.title: Arpeggiator never runs in ordinary play (held-note pool is a stale config snapshot)
issues.detail: synth-render.ts gates the arp on ctx.arpNotes.length > 0, and arpNotes comes from the backend config, which PianoEngine only refreshes in pushConfig() on a state change. noteOn updates arpHeldNotes but does not push config, so at the moment a voice is rendered the pool is whatever it was at the last panel interaction — empty in normal use. Measured: with ARP RUN engaged, a 3 s held note produced the same single-pulse envelope and identical peak (0.0934) as with the arp off, and moving the arp rate knob from 0 to 127 changed the detected pulse count only from 2 to 1. The mechanism itself works when forced: with KB HOLD holding C3+C5 and a panel toggle afterwards, 100 ms Goertzel tracking of 130.8 Hz and 523.3 Hz alternated cleanly, which is a real arpeggio. So the feature is present and unreachable through the interface a player uses.

issues.title: Rotary Speaker block missing from the performance band
issues.detail: The variant reference photograph shows a ROTARY SPEAKER block (ON, DRIVE, ORGAN, CLOSE MIC, STOP MODE, SLOW/FAST, MORPH) on the exposed red chassis at roughly x 2200-2500 of 11600, inside the 0-0.14 performance band, and specs/nord-stage-4.visual.json calls it out explicitly. The artifact's performance section contains only pitch stick, mod wheel, ctrl pedal, master level and branding; its rotary controls live in the organ and effects plates instead. This is the one missing landmark of the 33.

issues.title: 102 of 156 deck controls unreachable at 390x844
issues.detail: The instrument scales correctly at the narrow viewport (374.4 x 121.0, aspect 3.095, no horizontal overflow, all 73 keys playable), but the six deck sections keep overflow:hidden while their contents shrink, so the 5x5 elementFromPoint grid finds only 54/156 controls reachable: performance 4/4, organ 8/28, piano 3/15, program 10/29, synth 9/41, effects 20/39. Legends drop to 3px.

issues.title: Six controls partially clipped by their section at 1440x900
issues.detail: All six deck sections are overflow:hidden. The synth section's content is 250px tall inside a 227px box, leaving synth.unison, synth.glideRate and synth.vibrato only 29.3% visible; program.pageLeft/pageRight are 91.6% visible and program.dial 89.6%. Each still exposes a reachable grid point, so this costs nothing on the reachability measurement, but the panel visibly truncates.

issues.title: Keybed overhangs the chassis and the key fronts are cut off
issues.detail: The keybed rect ends at y 663.22 while the instrument ends at y 651.66 and .instrument is overflow:hidden, so the front 11.6px of every key is clipped by the chassis edge (visible in the cropped render). Key geometry itself is correct — 73 keys, 43 white / 30 black, all inside the keybed, black-key height fraction 0.6100.

issues.title: FX FOCUS A/B LEDs do not follow the engine's focused layer
issues.detail: Clicking piano.layerA / synth.layerB / organ.layerB sets engine.effects.focusSection and focusLayer (panel-bindings.ts pressFunctionalControl), and the section OLEDs follow, but the fx.focusA / fx.focusB buttons keep whatever state they were last clicked into: after clicking piano.layerA, fx.focusA still read aria-pressed=false and fx.focusB true. The FX FOCUS LEDs therefore point at the wrong layer whenever focus was changed from a section button.

issues.title: Arp/Gate mode renders digital silence at maximum rate
issues.detail: With the arp pool populated, arpMode = Gate and the ARP RATE knob at 127, a 3 s held note rendered exactly 0 in every 5 ms envelope bucket. The same configuration at the default rate 90 gated correctly (modulation at 3.6 Hz, depth 0.55), so the extreme end of the rate range collapses the gate to silence rather than to a fast chop.

issues.title: Unlabelled buttons and label/control collisions
issues.detail: Six buttons in the organ VIB/CHORUS · PERCUSSION row carry only LEDs and no silkscreen, so the vibrato selector and the three percussion switches are unidentifiable without the accessible name; the piano OCT button overlaps the MODEL knob and its legend is half-covered; the effects ROTARY group label sits on top of the ROTARY button.

issues.title: build/index.html is a fragment, so the page renders in quirks mode
issues.detail:
The published build/index.html contains only the module script tag, the stylesheet link and
— no doctype, , , or <body>. Chromium reports document.compatMode = 'BackCompat'. All measurements in this assessment were taken against exactly those bits. The page also has no document title.

issues.title: Sealed source carries a self-declared post-seal edit
issues.detail: src/audio/web-audio-backend.ts buildImpulse() opens with 'POST-SEAL FIX (disclosed in the evaluation report)', describing a rewrite of the reverb impulse construction from an O(n·k) direct convolution to an O(n) copy. Reported as an observation, not a judgement: the published build does contain the fixed version (measured reverb type changes block only 6.7-11.8 ms), so what I measured is internally consistent.

evidence: Measured in the published build at 1440x900 (getBoundingClientRect on [data-instrument], .deck, .keybed-wrap): instrument 1353.59 x 437.33 at x=43.20,y=214.33; deck height 236.16 -> deckFraction 0.539998; keybed-wrap height 201.16 -> keybedFraction 0.45997; widthFraction 1353.59/1440 = 0.93999; aspectRatio 1353.59/437.33 = 3.09514 vs spec 3.0951.

Six section slots measured against instrument width: performance 0.13677 (target 0.14), organ 0.19538 (0.20), piano 0.08303 (0.085), program 0.12387 (0.125), synth 0.24423 (0.25), effects 0.19538 (0.20). Worst deviation 0.00577 on synth, inside the 0.012 tolerance. The slots sum to 0.9787 rather than 1.0 because ~2.1% of the deck width goes to inter-section gaps, which is what biases every section slightly low.
The section fractions in artifact/src/hardware/variant.ts match the current spec values (0.14/0.20/0.085/0.125/0.25/0.20), not the superseded coarse values, and the rendered slots confirm it.

Reachability by the 5x5 elementFromPoint grid at 1440x900 with the page unscrolled (no framework click helper): all 156 [data-control-id] elements resolved to themselves or a descendant on at least one grid point, so 156/156. The instrument fits the viewport (body scrollHeight 900, no scroll).

Landmarks: 32 of the 33 sectionLandmarks entries are rendered in their own section. The one absent is 'rotary speaker controls' in the performance band: [data-section="performance"] contains exactly perf.pitchStick, perf.modWheel, perf.ctrlPedal, perf.masterLevel plus the STAGE 4 / NORD brand and a '73 · HAMMER ACTION' legend. The reference photo nord-stage-4-73.jpg shows a ROTARY SPEAKER block (ON, DRIVE, ORGAN, CLOSE MIC, STOP MODE, SLOW/FAST, MORPH) on the exposed red chassis at roughly x 2200-2500 of 11600, inside this band; this artifact puts its rotary controls in the organ and effects sections instead.

Forbidden elements: 0. performance carries no inset plate (no .inset class) and no OLED; organ's only display-ish element is a 14.7px-wide model-name span (0.056 of the section, not a wide OLED); piano has no display and no drawbar bank; exactly one primary OLED exists in program (0.952 of that section) and one in synth (0.254 of that section, not spanning it); effects has no OLED and is split into 7 labelled groups (EFFECT 1, EFFECT 2, AMP/EQ, DELAY, COMP, REVERB, ROTARY) rather than one undifferentiated grid.

Placement caveat measured but not charged twice: all six deck sections are overflow:hidden and the synth section's content is 250px tall in a 227px box, so synth.unison, synth.glideRate and synth.vibrato are only 29.3% visible (program.pageLeft/pageRight 91.6%, program.dial 89.6%). They still expose a reachable grid point, so they count as both present and reachable.

73 [data-key-id] buttons rendered: 43 .key-white, 30 .key-black. Every one of the 73 key boxes falls inside the [data-keybed] rect (49.28,468.83,1341.44x194.39) within 0.75px, so keysInsideKeybed = 73/73.

Median white key 31.19 x 194.39 px, median black key 19.33 x 118.58 px: black-key height fraction 118.58/194.39 = 0.6100 (target 0.61), black/white width ratio 0.620. Range is E1(28)-E7(100) per the keybed aria-label, matching the Stage 4 73 variant.

The keybed does overhang the chassis: keybed bottom 663.22 vs instrument bottom 651.66, and .instrument has overflow:hidden, so the front 11.6px of every key is cut off by the chassis edge (visible in scratch/probe-p3-crop.png).

Screenshot of the instrument bounding box (1354x437, 9404 unique colours) converted to CIE L*a*b*; nearest rendered surface of at least 200px per reference colour: chassisMid #851a25 deltaE 0.00 (rgb 133,26,37 / 3523px), chassisDark #5a0c13 deltaE 4.20 (86,16,23 / 490px), panelBlueGray #3c424d deltaE 0.44 (59,65,76 / 5763px), keyBlack #0b0b0b deltaE 0.00 (11,11,11 / 45569px), keyWhite #dcdcdc deltaE 0.00 (220,220,220 / 250px).

All five are inside deltaE 12, so 5/5 matched. Every reference colour also has an exact-hex pixel match somewhere in the render; the 200px surface floor was applied so anti-aliasing noise could not be counted as a surface.

Materials read as the hardware at 3x zoom (scratch/probe-p3-zoom-organ.png, probe-p3-zoom-fx.png): nine drawbars with off-white caps over 8-segment LED ladders, faders with their own ladders, knobs with a moulded body and a white pointer, buttons with a red LED plus a discrete option-LED row, dark blue-grey inset plates with a red perimeter on a red chassis, and two green-phosphor OLEDs carrying live text.

Silkscreen sizes measured in the rendered page: .ctl-legend is 6.912px and 5.76px; legends such as STRING RES, SUST PED, ARP RUN, MID FREQ and P.PONG are still readable in the 1x crop, and no legend element overflows its box (scrollWidth > clientWidth on 0 of them).

Simplifications a player would notice: six buttons in the organ VIB/CHORUS · PERCUSSION row carry no legend at all (only LEDs), the piano OCT button visually collides with the MODEL knob so its legend is half-covered, the effects ROTARY group label sits on top of its ROTARY button, and the bottom row of the synth section is cut off by the section's overflow:hidden.

Displays are live: the program OLED tracks position/name/dirty ('1.1 Grand Piano E' after changing piano type, back to '1.1 Grand Piano' after STORE, '1.3 B3 Jazz' on slot change, '2.1 Split Bass/Piano' after PAGE-right + program 1, 'Live 1 Init' in Live Mode), the clock line reads '120 BPM · TR +1 · SCENE I' and updates with transpose and scene, and the split-edit line reads position and crossfade.

Controls track their parameters: the synth.filterCutoff knob pointer transform goes from matrix(-0.707,-0.707,0.707,-0.707) at aria-valuenow 0 to matrix(-0.707,0.707,-0.707,-0.707) at 127, and the synth OLED simultaneously reads 'LP12 F127 R0 · ENV A 0.0 D 10.0 R 1.9'. Section OLEDs follow layer focus: clicking synth.layerB switched the synth OLED from 'A · Saw · OSC CTRL 0.0' to 'B · Saw ...' and clicking organ.layerB switched the organ label from 'A: B3' to 'B: B3'. Morph assignment lit [data-morph-led="piano.level"], and the zone keys relabel to 'Zone 1 (E1–C4)' / 'Zone 2 (C4–E7)' when split is engaged.

Two state displays are untruthful. The FX FOCUS A/B buttons never follow the engine's focused layer: after clicking piano.layerA (which sets effects.focusSection='piano', focusLayer='A') fx.focusA still read aria-pressed=false and fx.focusB stayed true. And the rotary ON / SLOW-FAST LEDs light while the rotary unit produces no change in the rendered signal at all (see the rotary issue), so the panel reports an engaged effect that is not in the graph.

At 390x844 the instrument stays recognisable and the keybed stays playable: bounding box 374.4 x 121.0, width fraction 0.960, aspect 3.095 (unchanged), body scrollWidth 390 = innerWidth so nothing overflows horizontally, all 73 keys resolve under elementFromPoint, and a real pointer press on the D4 key rendered audio (rms 0.0626, peak 0.2805).

The deck, however, mostly stops working: the same 5x5 elementFromPoint grid finds only 54 of 156 controls reachable — performance 4/4, organ 8/28, piano 3/15, program 10/29, synth 9/41, effects 20/39 — because the sections keep overflow:hidden while their content is scaled down, and .ctl-legend drops to 3px, below readable size.
